planning_notes: Circuit uses a pulldown resistor: D4 reads HIGH when the button is pressed (connected to 5V) and LOW when not pressed (held to GND through 10kΩ). Therefore digital_input active_high is true and model 'true' corresponds to HIGH at D4.

Serial output requires printing exact fixed lines. Two serial_text_output requests are provided for exact strings 'Button pressed' and 'Button not pressed'; SysML will set the corresponding gates based on the sampled button state.
Framing is assumed to follow the provided default (line_or_idle, idle_timeout_ms=20). No explicit serial command inputs are required.
No other wired electrical pins are present beyond the pushbutton on D4; no additional GPIO/PWM/analog/DHT/ultrasonic/servo/display ports are requested.

interfaces.name: io_0
interfaces.meaning: Button pressed state (HIGH when pressed, LOW when not pressed)

interfaces.name: io_1
interfaces.meaning: Serial gate: print fixed line 'Button pressed' when button is pressed

interfaces.name: io_2
interfaces.meaning: Serial gate: print fixed line 'Button not pressed' when button is not pressed

interfaces.name: serial_0_trigger
interfaces.meaning: Gate for 'Button pressed' vs 'Button not pressed' fixed-text reporting derived from the button model state

interfaces.name: serial_0_value_0
interfaces.meaning: Button model state used to select between the two fixed serial text lines

configuration_resolution.original_requirement:
# Button Pulldown

## Project Description
This is a simple Arduino project that prints whether the button is pressed.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- 10kΩ resistor
- Push Button

## Circuit Description
Circuit is designed to use a pull-down resistor. When the button is not pressed, the pin4 pin is connected to gnd2 through a 10kΩ resistor. When the button is pressed, the pin4 pin is connected to 5V.

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Initialize serial communication
2. Configure the specified button pin as INPUT
3. Continuously check the button value, and print "Button pressed" if the value is HIGH, or print "Button not pressed" if the value is LOW.

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. "Button pressed" is printed when the button is pressed
2. "Button not pressed" is printed when the button is not pressed

## Notes for Implementation
- The pin number used should match the circuit diagram
- When the button is not pressed, pin1.l is connected to pin1.r and pin2.l is connected to pin2.r. When the button is pressed, all the pins are connected together.

## Variants
This project may have different variants with the pushbutton connected to different pins.

## Attributes
- To use 10kΩ resistor, set the property name "value" to "10000 ohm".
Given circuit (must preserve wiring):
{
    "version": 1,
    "author": "Blind Author",
    "description": "Manage pull down registor button input",
    "config": {
        "button_pin": 4,
        "gnd_pin": "GND.2"
    },
    "parts": [
        {
            "type": "wokwi-arduino-uno",
            "id": "arduino uno1",
            "top": 0,
            "left": 0,
            "attrs": {}
        },
        {
            "type": "wokwi-pushbutton",
            "id": "push button1",
            "top": -144.6,
            "left": 70.2,
            "rotate": 90,
            "attrs": {
                "color": "green",
                "xray": "1"
            }
        },
        {
            "type": "wokwi-resistor",
            "id": "resistor1",
            "top": -63.25,
            "left": 38.4,
            "attrs": {
                "value": "10000"
            }
        }
    ],
    "connections": [
        [
            "resistor1:2",
            "push button1:2.r",
            "green",
            [
                "v0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "resistor1:1",
            "arduino uno1:GND.2",
            "green",
            [
                "v0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "push button1:2.l",
            "arduino uno1:4",
            "green",
            [
                "v0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "push button1:1.r",
            "arduino uno1:5V",
            "green",
            [
                "v0"
            ]
        ]
    ],
    "dependencies": {}
}
